notes:
Two concurrent muse REPL sessions launched in the SAME cwd via the interactive driver's start_session step. Each muse process mints its OWN session UUID as its session-directory basename (session_id = dir basename, format-spec §1), so the two distinct session_ids are asserted via new_session/same_session_as relations, not literal ids. s1_session_birth is the one unpinned phase (nothing earlier exists to pin to) and anchors on 'ready', not 'working': muse's process scanner (CommandPattern, wired unconditionally in cmd/irrlichd/wiring.go) emits a transient proc-<PID> presession row also born in ready, but empirically (verified directly against this recording's own raw events, and independently against the model-identification cell's recording too) the REAL top-level session's ready fires BEFORE its own proc-<PID> shadow's -- session1's real ready at 06:04:09.211598 precedes proc-53461's at 06:04:09.451629 here, matching the same ordering independently confirmed for a different cell's recording.

SCOPE NOTE -- session 1's turn 1 is sent by the recipe (as documented behavior) but is NOT independently phase-verified here, and that is deliberate, not an oversight: session 1 hits the SAME pre-existing daemon bug the #1960 onboarding brief pre-identified (post-birth transcript churn -- a transcript_removed fires ~0.28s after birth, causing re-discovery and loss of prev_state on the next transition), directly confirmed in this recording's raw events (transcript_new 06:04:09.207 -> transcript_removed 06:04:09.484 -> a second 'new session created' ready at 06:04:21.009 -- a re-discovery, not a real completion) -- session 1's real id NEVER gets a working transition for turn 1 anywhere in the capture. A first live attempt at this cell (before this spec existed) vacuously PASSED a turn1-verifying phase by matching a reminder-agent SUBAGENT's own working->ready cycle instead (session_id 4801192e-...) -- exactly the vacuous-pass risk this whole onboarding pass was briefed to check for. A corrected same_session_as-pinned retry then found session 1's real id has exactly ONE working transition in the whole recording (turn 2's, at 06:04:44.911539) -- pinning a 'turn1' phase to it would have mislabeled turn 2's data as turn 1's, which is worse than an honest gap. So this spec tests what IS cleanly, correctly observable: session 2's independent birth+turn (assertions 2) and session 1's SECOND turn while session 2 is alive (assertion 3, the scenario's actual point -- PID-to-session binding stability). Not a new issue -- one of the two pre-identified daemon bugs, no issue filed.

s2_birth carries min_delay_ms:15000 alongside new_session:true: without the floor, the SAME subagent contamination hits s2_birth too -- session 1's turn-1 reminder subagents reach their own 'working' at 06:04:13.78 (only ~4.5s after s1_session_birth), which also satisfies a bare new_session search (subagents are never matched by an earlier phase, so they always look 'new'). The floor skips past that window; session 2's real working at 06:04:40.50 (31.3s after anchor) is the next candidate with nothing else in between. Tokens are durably persisted (model_completed.usage, format-spec §6) so tokens_nonzero is asserted true; no cost field exists anywhere in the corpus and muse's model has no aliases.go pricing entry, so cost_nonzero is asserted false, not left unset.

text: Session 1 appears in ready (the sole unpinned identity anchor -- verified against this recording's raw events to precede its own proc-<PID> presession shadow)

Session 2 starts in the SAME cwd as a DISTINCT session_id and reaches working on its own first prompt (new_session proves it is not session 1; min_delay_ms skips past session 1's turn-1 reminder-subagent working transitions, which would otherwise also satisfy new_session; anchoring on working skips session 2's own proc-<PID> placeholder)
Session 2 first turn completes: working -> ready -- independent of session 1

Session 1 is driven AGAIN while session 2 is still alive -- a working transition on session 1's original session_id proves the .session.lock-based PID binding stayed stable and did not flap to session 2's PID. This is the scenario's actual point. Session 1's real id has exactly one working transition in the whole recording, so this phase (pinned same_session_as s1_session_birth) unambiguously identifies it as this second turn's.
